patch.value: The fleet's own mandatory gates as the first sim-to-RL environment

The honest version of recursive self-improvement for this ecosystem is not a claim about general capability, it is a measurable loop the fleet already runs by hand. An agent proposes a change to a pm package; the package's own mandatory gates decide whether it passed. Those gates are unusually well suited to being a reward because they were built to be uncheatable for a different reason: exact coverage thresholds, docstring coverage, acceptance scripts that run the built artifact, and bot review rounds that must be resolved rather than dismissed. The environment is the repository at a pinned commit, the action is a diff, and the reward is the gate verdict, which is already deterministic and already recorded. Registering that as a pm-rl environment turns the fleet's own review history into training and evaluation data with complete provenance, and it makes the sim-to-real gap concrete: gate-pass rate in the sandboxed environment against merge rate on real pull requests.

The environment specification pins the repository commit, the gate command set, and the verdict extraction, and is content-addressed like every other environment; a recorded episode replays to the same verdict on the same commit; the sim-to-real report contrasts sandbox gate-pass rate with real pull-request merge rate over the same period; no episode captures repository credentials or hosted service data

patch.value: The environment specification pins the repository commit, the gate command set and the verdict extraction, and is content-addressed like every other environment; a recorded episode stores a content-addressed identity for the candidate tree, not only the base commit, and replay resolves that exact artifact; a replayed episode produces the same verdict; each sandbox episode carries a stable link to its corresponding pull request; the sim-to-real gap is computed over the paired cohort present on both sides with the denominator stated, and unpaired candidates are reported separately as coverage rather than folded into a rate; no episode captures repository credentials or hosted service data

The honest version of recursive self-improvement for this ecosystem is not a claim about general capability, it is a measurable loop the fleet already runs by hand. An agent proposes a change to a pm package; the package's own mandatory gates decide whether it passed. Those gates are unusually well suited to being a reward because they were built to be uncheatable for a different reason: exact coverage thresholds, docstring coverage, acceptance scripts that run the built artifact, and bot review rounds that must be resolved rather than dismissed. The environment specification pins the repository commit, but a commit identifies only the base tree and the episode's action is a diff, so the commit alone does not identify what was actually judged. The episode therefore records a content-addressed identity for the candidate tree itself - the resulting tree id, or the patch that produces it - and replay resolves that exact artifact before running the gates. Without it, replay reruns the gates against a tree it merely hopes is the same one. The sim-to-real gap needs the same discipline on the comparison itself. Sandbox gate-pass rate and real merge rate over the same period are not comparable when they draw on different candidate populations, so each sandbox episode is linked to the pull request it corresponds to and the gap is reported over the paired cohort of candidates that appear on both sides, with the denominator stated. Candidates present on only one side are reported separately as coverage rather than being silently folded into a rate.

message: Content-address the candidate tree and define the paired cohort for the sim-to-real gap
